blockers.title: The specification's matrix and global pass property quantify over 'supported filesystems', a set that exists nowhere in this corpus; the file populates nothing, books nothing, and the one pointer it offers routes to a different question at a different gate
blockers.location: matrix, filesystems, passProperty, and EV-1/EV-2/EV-4 exactByteIntent
blockers.finding: The matrix field reads 'hostile archive/path/loader/TOCTOU corpus on supported filesystems × the four D-002 platforms' and the global passProperty asserts that each member's pass property 'holds on every D-002 platform and supported filesystem'. Three of the four members repeat 'per D-002 platform and supported filesystem' inside their exactByteIntent. One of those two axes has a decided domain and the other does not. The platform axis resolves: D-002 fixes macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64, arm64), the file names all four, and the register's waiver clause — 'waiver requires platform removal' — gives that axis its only lawful escape. The filesystem axis resolves to nothing. I searched the whole corpus: the phrase 'supported filesystem' occurs in exactly one live governing place, the DR-G07 register cell this file is authored against, and not one filesystem type token — APFS, HFS+, ext4, XFS, btrfs, ZFS — appears anywhere in docs/v2 or in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS. The set is undefined, and the file's own filesystems field concedes it: 'This specification does not populate a filesystem allowlist.' Conceding it would be fine if the file then booked the gap. It does not. proposedLaterWork carries five items — fixture authoring, qualification execution, platform removal, the DR-103 leftovers, and the deferred SATISFIED-GRADE cycle — and none of them is the filesystem enumeration. Nothing in whatThisCloses names it. So the specification ships a matrix with an axis of unknown cardinality and no owner. What the file offers instead is a pointer, and the pointer is wrong: 'TCB filesystem selectors remain RESERVED as G22 evidence.' TCB v45's filesystem selectors are platformProfile selection keys — a filesystemTypeToken derived from macOS statfs or Linux mountinfo to identify which profile an install root sits on — and its populationPacket entry says 'This contract authors the grammar, including version/build and filesystem selectors, and does not populate them... This row does not name, designate, or claim independent review of that later packet. Choosing its owner is a separate decision.' That is a TCB profile-keying question, not G07's coverage domain, and DR-G22's own live cell carries its own unenumerated 'supported OS/filesystem/architecture' axis, so G22 is not a place where G07's answer is waiting. There is direct precedent that this gap is finding-grade rather than housekeeping: the independent Codex review of platform-tcb-contract.v2 raised exactly it — 'The recorded file-04, file-08, and COORD sources contain none of APFS, HFS+, ext4, or XFS' — with the impact 'No complete active profile exists to key an allowlist entry or drive the G22 matrix.' TCB answered by declaring the selectors RESERVED, marking requiredBeforeAllowlistFreeze true, and booking a later population packet. This candidate faces the same gap and books nothing.
blockers.whyItMatters: The register's threshold is 'pass all', and the only waiver it grants is platform removal — there is no filesystem escape hatch, no skipped-cell provision, and the file's own passProperty reinforces this with 'Waiver of a platform is platform removal, not a skipped cell.' With the filesystem axis undefined, 'pass all' is neither achievable nor falsifiable: a qualification cycle could run the corpus on one filesystem per platform and claim the matrix, or a reviewer could reject the same run as incomplete, and this specification decides neither. That is the one thing a specification of exact-byte intent exists to settle, and it is settled for the platform axis three sentences earlier.
blockers.corroboratingDetail: The file's handling of this axis is not even internally consistent. EV-1, EV-2 and EV-4 each say 'per D-002 platform and supported filesystem'; EV-3 says only 'per D-002 platform', dropping the axis without saying why, although file 04's DR-G07 sentence puts loader and entrypoint replacement inside the same 'across supported platforms/filesystems' scope as everything else, and the global passProperty then re-asserts the filesystem quantifier over all four members including EV-3.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Either enumerate the domain from a live source if one can be found — I could not find one — or, far more likely, do what TCB v45 did with the same gap: state that the supported-filesystem set is UNPOPULATED, name it as a remaining obligation with the act that must supply it, mark the matrix incomplete until then, and quantify the pass property over the platform axis alone until the set exists. Either way EV-3's dropped qualifier should be reconciled with EV-1/EV-2/EV-4 and with the global pass property.

shouldFix.title: EV-2 makes pathRule / RJ-3 load-bearing for its Unicode-alias limb without disclosing that the join it cites records that exact rule as BLOCKED for the Unicode case pending a schema successor
shouldFix.location: retainedEvidence[1] measures / exactByteIntent / passProperty, against basedOn.leftoverJoinV2
shouldFix.finding: EV-2 states 'This member consumes pathRule / RJ-3', quotes the pathRule uniqueness clause including 'unique under case-folding and Unicode normalization', and passes on 'Two aliases (case, Unicode, or link) cannot execute different bytes than the verified tree. pathRule violations refuse as executed-tree identity failure.' The D-161 join this candidate names as basedOn, at a digest I reproduced, records the opposite standing for that rule's Unicode limb: OBL-UNICODE-NORM reads 'v6: TC-PATH unicode-norm-duplicate is BLOCKED on schemas.v11 pathRule / RJ-3. A later schema successor is required before this member can be scored.' So the corpus has already recorded that pathRule / RJ-3 as it stands cannot score the Unicode-normalization-duplicate class, and EV-2 consumes it as live law for precisely that class without a word about the block. The candidate's disclosure stops one hop short: it says 'OBL-UNICODE-NORM and OBL-WINDOWS-PATH remain on DR-103', which tells a reader the obligation is not closed here but not that the rule this member consumes is recorded as unable to score one of the three alias limbs it names. I considered and rejected the defence that the two questions are different — the DR-103 class is manifest-admission and EV-2's is executed-tree behaviour — because EV-2 does not confine itself to filesystem behaviour: its second pass sentence makes pathRule enforcement itself part of the G07 pass property, and its exactByteIntent retains 'refusal records for pathRule violations at extract/exec'.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: This specification exists to tell a later fixture-authoring cycle what to build. A known blocker sitting under one of its three alias limbs is exactly what that cycle needs told, and it is the kind of thing that is expensive to rediscover after fixtures are half-authored.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Add one sentence to EV-2 recording that the Unicode limb's consumed rule is BLOCKED per D-161 / OBL-UNICODE-NORM pending a schemas successor, and say whether the executed-tree Unicode limb is scorable without that successor or waits on it.

shouldFix.title: EV-3 measures runtime-library resolution inside the verified tree, retains no evidence of it, and disclaims the one evidence form that would witness it without naming where the property is witnessed instead
shouldFix.finding: EV-3's measures field takes file 04's fifth binding bullet whole: 'Entrypoint and runtime-library resolution inside the verified tree.' Its exactByteIntent then enumerates what is retained — the verified tree digest, the descriptor or open-handle identity or digest-recheck record, 'the executed entrypoint path and digest', and refusal records for the substitution classes. Nothing in that list is a resolution record: no list of what the spawned process actually loaded, and no statement of whether the digest recheck is scoped to the entrypoint or to the whole tree. The passProperty then closes the only door left with 'G22 retained loader traces are not this member.' Read together, EV-3 asserts a property about where the loader looked and what it found, retains bytes that establish what the tree contained and which entrypoint ran, and pushes away the artifact that would connect the two. The gap is narrower than it first looks, which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker: DR-G22's live evidence cell is 'full loader trace, identity/version allowlist, ...', and a full trace would show in-tree library resolution, so the evidence plausibly exists at G22. But G22's claim is about declared platform TCB dependencies — libc, framework, cert store, font, ICU — not about a component's own in-tree libraries, and this file's g22Split describes G22's scope in exactly those terms. So the candidate tells the reader what this member is not, and never what the runtime-library limb of its own measures is.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Either retain the resolution evidence here — say the digest recheck is tree-scoped, or pin the resolved runtime-library set against TreeCommitment entries — or route the limb explicitly, in the idiom the file already uses well for AT-8, the 51 fixtures and the TCB paragraph: name G22's full loader trace as where in-tree runtime-library resolution is witnessed, rather than only disclaiming it.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 3 SHOULD-FIX. Eighteen attacks run, two landed. Custody holds at both ends: subject a93b38d0 at 0444, 15554 bytes, unmoved and unedited; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 is 3a9442d1 and equals the subject's own pin; required-now reads 26 of 26 live. All seven cited digests reproduce. I want to be plain that most of this candidate is very good. Five register cells are character-exact against the row located by ID; all four live members are present with an exactByteIntent, a passProperty and a not-authored suppliedBy; every exactByteIntent is guarded 'Once authored:' and closes 'Fixtures are unauthored.'; and the corpus classes are explicitly not invented FX/AT/TC identifiers. The boundary work reproduces from its sources: seventeen AT-ARCHIVE-* member keys, all classed AT-8, executing at DR-G15; the six-member DR-103 leftover set matching the D-161 join exactly; the TCB paragraph and loader-trace allowlist left to G22/DR-126 with verifiedInstallRoot correctly described as riding this gate; admission identity left as plain sha256 with the signing preimage on ID-DEP-1 and no canonicalization invented. The authority citation most worth breaking — D-056 turn-2 Decision clause 5 — reproduces word for word from the pinned turn-2 subject. All seven file-04 binding bullets and all six DR-G07 coverage items are accounted for, and the one bullet not taken is DR-103's own live acceptance-evidence cell. It fails on one axis. The file's matrix is 'corpus on supported filesystems × the four D-002 platforms' and its global pass property is quantified over 'every D-002 platform and supported filesystem'. The platform axis has a decided domain at D-002 and a lawful escape in the register's platform-removal waiver. The filesystem axis has neither. The phrase occurs in exactly one live governing place — the DR-G07 cell this file is authored against — and no filesystem type token appears anywhere in docs/v2 or COORD. The file concedes it populates nothing, books the gap in no later-work item, and offers a pointer that mis-routes: TCB v45's filesystem selectors are profile-keying tokens the TCB contract explicitly declines to populate, with its owner undecided, and DR-G22 carries its own unenumerated filesystem axis. There is precedent that this is finding-grade — the independent Codex review of platform-tcb-contract.v2 raised the identical absence, and TCB answered by declaring the selectors RESERVED and booking a population packet. This candidate faces it and books nothing, so 'pass all' at a gate with no filesystem waiver is neither achievable nor falsifiable as specified. The three SHOULD-FIX items are each one sentence of repair: a truncated TCB quotation that drops the DR-103 co-owner from the boundary sentence, an EV-2 Unicode limb resting on a rule the cited join records as BLOCKED pending a schema successor, and an EV-3 that measures runtime-library resolution, retains no resolution evidence, and disclaims loader traces without saying where that limb is witnessed. One procedural item for you rather than a finding: OBL-G07-HARNESS-SPEC exists nowhere in the corpus except this candidate and this cycle's prompt. Unlike its G12 and G21 siblings it was created by no recorded join and has no architecture-row home, and the candidate books it on the gate row.
